page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Furbo Mini 360° on day one: $35 camera + $83.92 Nanny Standard = $118.92, which is $18.92 over a $100 budget. Every option shown on Furbo's page includes a plan.
  • Petcube Bites 2 Lite with no plan: $99.99 + $0 = $99.99. Live view stays on Petcube's free tier.
  • Petcube with recorded clips, bundle route: $0 camera + $9.99 × 12 months = $119.88.
  • Petcube with recorded clips, bought outright: $99.99 + $59.88 Optimal yearly = $159.87.
  • Treat hopper: the Mini 360° holds 10 treats against the Furbo 360°'s 100, a tenth as many (Furbo's own chart).
  • Treat size: Petcube takes treats up to 1 in; the Mini 360° tops out at 0.5 in, so 1 ÷ 0.5 = twice the largest treat.
If you wantPick
Live view, talk-back and treat tossing with no monthly billPetcube Bites 2 Lite
Recorded clips with no plan feeTKENPRO 2K (microSD)
A camera that pans to follow your petTKENPRO 2K (355° pan)
Large dog treats up to 1 inchPetcube Bites 2 Lite
Small round cat treats, and you want a Nanny plan anywayFurbo Mini 360°

What each camera really costs in year one

Every camera on this list streams live video. They differ in whether recorded clips need a subscription and how long that subscription locks you in.

Petcube sells the Bites 2 Lite two ways. Bought outright at $99.99, it keeps live streaming on the free Basic tier, which Petcube says comes with every camera. Care Optimal adds 3-day history and Smart Alerts for $59.88 a year. The Care Bundle gives you the camera for $0, but the plan must renew for at least 12 months. Cancel early or miss a payment and you owe $99.95 for the camera. After 12 months, cancelling turns off history and Smart Alerts, and live streaming keeps working. WIRED's tester, Molly Higgins, notes that the Bites 2 Lite lets you set both the amount and the distance of each toss. {buy:petcube-bites-2-lite}

Furbo lists the Mini 360° at $35 (crossed-out $99), but the cart adds Nanny Standard billed at $83.92. Furbo's terms set a minimum of three continuous months, say subscription payments are nonrefundable, and say that once a plan ends you only get the real-time stream, with no past recordings. Furbo's help center adds that Subscription-Required units lock live view until a plan is linked. WIRED's Molly Higgins found the Mini 360° can't schedule feedings or change the amount dispensed.

TKENPRO records to a microSD card. TheConsumers.guide says that lets you record continuously without paying anyone monthly, so year one costs the camera plus a card. WIRED's tester could schedule regular feedings with it and found the video never laggy. {buy:tkenpro-2k-pet-camera-treat-dispenser}

Not recommended

Furbo Mini 360° at its $35 headline price. For a $100 budget it comes to $118.92 at Furbo's checkout. Its hopper holds up to 10 small treats, round and 0.25–0.5 in (Furbo), and the plan can't be refunded for the first three months. It fits only a shopper who already wants a Furbo Nanny plan and uses small cat-sized treats.
